docs.text: The Frozen Wastes Written by: Professor Grunkle Blinkfizzle Foreword by Professor Grunkle Blinkfizzle (Fellow of the Sylvanian Institute of Arcane) Ah! You’ve found it — my humble compendium of curious exploits, obscure creatures, and exceedingly brave (and occasionally foolish) souls. Splendid! What you hold in your hands is no mere storybook, dear reader. It is an account . A scholarly work! (Well, mostly scholarly.) In these pages I endeavor to record the true and terrible Tale of the Frozen Three — a fellowship bound not by destiny (though it seems to have had an opinion on the matter), but by circumstance, courage, and a most inconvenient frost. You shall meet Aronious , the ranger who turned his back on the gods to chase redemption in the snow; Yin Shen , a clever and wily kitsune rogue whose smile hides more than her daggers; and Hobbins , a wizard whose knack for mischief rivals his arcane prowess — heroes, villains, beasts, and beings best left unnamed before dusk. Expect here a union of two disciplines: The academic , wherein I catalogue beasts, plants, relics, and ruins for the enrichment of the Sylvanian archives; and The adventurous , wherein I recount their deeds with as much accuracy as my ink and sanity can afford. So! Read on, brave scholar or idle wanderer. Take notes if you wish (I do). Laugh when the absurd demands it, and tremble when the ice bites deep. Within these tales lie lessons on courage, folly, friendship, and the curious resilience of mortals when the world itself turns cold. Now then — my tea grows tepid, and the yeti bones won’t articulate themselves. Let us begin. docs.text: Crafting Players can craft items and equipment, both magical and mundane. Should they desire to be in control of their character progression. Requirements Just like in real life, your player character will need to satisfy pre-requisites in order to craft. You will need: ability tools materials time Tools You must use the required tool to make an item and have proficiency with that tool. Anyone who helps you must also have proficiency with it. Materials To make an item, you need raw materials. The DM will supply a list of necessary raw materials for the crafting of the requested item. Not all materials are readily available even in well connected or highly populated city centers. Some are just simply not available due to difficulty. Players will need to venture out to locations where they can find the materials and gather it themselves. Time Players must dedicate time to the endeavor of creating the item. If an item requires multiple days, the days needn’t be consecutive. Characters can combine their efforts to shorten the crafting time. Divide the time needed to create an item by the number of characters working on it. Normally, only one other character can assist you, but the DM might allow more assistants. Magic Items To create magic items you must follow the requirements laid out above for normal or mundane items along with all the requirements for magic items. Arcana Proficiecy To craft a magic item, you and any assistants must have proficiency in the Arcana skill. Spells If a magic item allows its user to cast any spells from it, you must have all those spells prepared every day you spend crafting the item.

docs.text: Session 1: The Blade in the Snow The tale begins in the frozen town of Bryn Shander , where the wind never ceases and hope flickers like a dying hearth. Within the stout walls of The Northlook Inn , travelers gathered to warm their bones and share rumor. Among them that night were three figures who, by fate or folly, would soon be bound by blood and ice. First was Aronious , a man of quiet strength — a ranger who once bore the light of the gods, now dimmed by his own choosing. He had walked the lonely paths of the tundra, seeking the freedom of one. That one was Yin Shen , a fox-spirited trickster of celestial origin — fallen, imprisoned, and marked by the goddess Auril’s endless Rime . Now fallen and bound to mortal flesh, her golden eyes and sharp grin betrayed a spark of the divine mischief that had once lit the heavens. And lastly, there was Hobbins , scarcely taller than a sword, a ferret of remarkable intellect and no patience whatsoever. She claimed to be a wizard — and though many laughed, none laughed long once she’d proven it. The three had scarcely entered The Northlook when their arrival drew the eye of Hiln Trollbane , a stout shield dwarf whose gaze carried the weight of suspicion and opportunity. When approached, she spoke of grim tidings — Over shared ale and cautious words, Hiln spoke of Sephek Kaltro , a blue-eyed killer she had stalked through Ten-Towns. He was said to be bound to Torg's Trading Company and to serve some darker purpose beneath the Frostmaiden’s will. Sensing both coin and cause, the trio agreed to take up the hunt. They left Bryn Shander along the The Eastway , snow crunching beneath their boots and paws, until the lights of the Trail’s End Tavern came into view. Within, the hum of travelers and traders mingled with the scent of wet wool and pine smoke. Aronious , ever cautious, circled the building, eyes sharp. He saw Torg’s caravan settled within — ten rooms in all — and one, curiously, with its window unlatched and footprints fresh in the snow. Hobbins , ever the opportunist, made herself scarce and soon reappeared with a few extra coins jingling in her pouch. Yin Shen , meanwhile, listened for whispers of the murderer among the merchants of Torg’s . The trio joined in a game of cards, wagering gold for gossip — and though they won, their questions drew suspicion. When the traders made to leave, Hobbins’ whiskers twitched with mischief. A quick spell, a whispered word, and one of the merchants turned back with an unnaturally friendly smile. Under the charm, he revealed what the others would not — that Sephek Kaltro was indeed among them, sleeping in one of the rented rooms, his demeanor cold and eyes ever-glowing blue. Hobbins , ever practical, also ensured her winnings were returned before the charm faded. The companions retired for the night, though none slept easily. Before dawn, they rose and crept toward Sephek’s chamber. Yin Shen’s deft hands found the lock pliant, and with a quiet click , the door swung inward — only to reveal an empty room, snow swirling through an open window. Without hesitation, they followed the trail into the blizzard. The footprints led them deep into a forest glade, where pines groaned under the weight of endless winter. There, bathed in moonlight like a phantom of the frost, stood Sephek Kaltro — his blade drawn, poised above a trembling Chwinga , one of the rare elemental spirits of Icewind Dale. The confrontation was swift and fierce. Magic sparked. Blades flashed. Aronious fought and was felled; Yin Shen’s daggers danced like silvered shadows; Hobbins unleashed bursts of flame, her tail whipping in delight and terror. Sephek moved with inhuman grace, his strikes fueled by something colder than hatred — until, at last, the light in his eyes dimmed. As his body fell, it melted into the snow, leaving behind only his blade — now shattered, yet alive with a darkness that drank the moonlight itself. The shards drew together, fusing into a dagger whose edge shimmered with an eerie, black anti-glow, as if even the darkness feared to touch it. Yin Shen reached for it, and though it burned cold in her palm, it did not harm her. The weapon pulsed once — as if recognizing her fallen divinity — and then fell silent.

docs.text: Session 10: The Gnome's Brother and the Race to the Trout After the chaos of the Duergar's capture, the party returned to The White Lady Inn for some well-needed rest. Over breakfast, Yin Shen asked the innkeeper about the leader of all Ten-Towns. The innkeeper explained that Danneth Waylen was the Speaker of Easthaven — though each town had its own speaker, and no single ruler governed them all. Hobbins , ever practical, asked a halfling attendant where one might get a drink at this early hour. The woman remarked that it was very early, but The Wet Trout — a seedier establishment — might already be serving. At the town hall, Captain Imdra Arlaggath met them with questions. She asked if they had any knowledge of why the Duergar would steal the Chardalyn crystal. Yin Shen told her everything — the prophecy from Hethyl Arkorran , the vision of a crystal machine with a dragon's heart, the warning that it could burn away the Rime and everything else with it. Imdra listened, her expression grim, but ultimately shook her head. She found it all hard to believe. Without proof, she could not bring such wild claims before the Speaker. Frustrated, Yin Shen descended to the basement to investigate the Duergar's cell. The dust was disturbed where the dwarf had been thrown in, and clear signs of struggle marked the floor. Then she saw it — footprints leading toward the door, each one progressively smaller than the last, until they vanished entirely at the threshold. The Duergar had escaped. The party left Easthaven and trekked back to Lupine's cave. The great dire wolf godling greeted them warmly, his wounds visibly healed since their last meeting. They recounted everything that had transpired with Skree — the battle, the corruption, the dark totem they had found. Yin Shen asked if Lupine would accompany them as a companion on their travels. Lupine's eyes softened, but he shook his massive head. "I am needed here," he rumbled. "My domain requires me. But know this — you have proven yourselves, and you have earned my friendship. Should you face a threat too great to bear alone, call upon me. I will come." Then, as a boon for their service, Lupine rose to his full height. A subtle blue glow began to emanate from his form, casting long shadows across the cave walls. He instructed the party to hold their weapons aloft. They did. Lupine exhaled, and frozen air poured from his maw like winter's breath made manifest. The fog coalesced on their weapons, forming delicate ice crystals that glimmered in the dim light before fading into the steel and wood. They had been blessed by a godling. The party returned to Easthaven and made their way to Strings and Sundries . A new sign hung on the door: "UNDR NEU MENAGAMENT" — misspelled, but unmistakable. Inside, they greeted Polard Hinscrop , who explained with several conspiratorial winks that he had "sold" the shop to his "brother." This way, both shops could operate as a single business, and he no longer needed the two-gnome charade. He added, still winking, that his "brother" was leaving town. Aronious — still blissfully unaware of the gnome's duplicitous nature — immediately rushed to the other shop to say goodbye to "Finkle." When he arrived at Drums Emporium , he heard a commotion from the back room. Moments later, the gnome emerged, a bead of sweat on his brow and wearing a freshly changed shirt. Aronious asked about the departure. The gnome explained he was leaving for the south — tired of the cold, homesick, eager to return to warmer lands. Aronious was so saddened by this news that he pleaded with "Finkle" to join the party on their adventures instead. After a long and absurd discussion between Aronious and "Finkle Shortfuse," it was agreed: by the next day, the gnome would be ready to set out with the party. After regrouping and catching up on Aronious' visit to the "other" music shop, Hobbins let out a deep sigh. She was growing bored traveling around with nothing to do. Not even a drop of Firebrandy to keep her occupied. The moment she saw her chance, she leapt from Aronious' shoulder, squeaking with joy. "Sorry, guys! I need a drink! I'm off to The Wet Trout! Last one there is a rotten egg! " And she bolted. What followed was utter chaos. Hobbins shot down the snow-dusted street like a streak of white fur, her tiny legs churning impossibly fast. Aronious, determined not to be a rotten egg, immediately tripped Yin Shen as she lunged forward. She tumbled face-first into a snowdrift with a muffled curse, scrambled to her feet, and gave chase with murder in her eyes. Aronious vaulted over a stack of fish crates at the corner, his boots barely touching the wood before he launched himself upward. He muttered the words to jump , and the spell took hold — propelling him twenty feet into the air. He landed hard on a snow-covered rooftop, tiles clattering beneath him, and took off at a dead sprint across the peaks of Easthaven. Below, Hobbins darted between the legs of a startled fishmonger, who dropped his basket with a shout. She leapt onto a rain barrel, then a windowsill, then the lip of a wagon bed, using each surface like a stepping stone. Behind her, Yin Shen wove through the crowd with practiced grace, dodging startled townsfolk and sliding beneath a cart loaded with firewood. Aronious reached the edge of a roof and didn't slow. He flung out his hand, and his thorn whip snapped forward, coiling around a chimney across the street. He swung through the air like a pendulum, boots skimming over the heads of confused pedestrians, and landed in a roll on the opposite rooftop. Hobbins saw the tavern in the distance and grinned. She thrust her paws forward and shouted the incantation for thunderwave . The blast erupted beneath her, launching her into the air in a wild, tumbling arc. She sailed over a stack of lumber, spun twice, and landed hard on the cobblestones — but kept running, her momentum barely broken. Yin Shen shifted mid-stride. Her body rippled and shrank, fur spreading across her limbs as she transformed into a fox. In the same breath, she conjured her mage hand — a shimmering spectral grip that seized her by the scruff and lifted her into the air. She flew forward like an arrow, weaving between clotheslines and over awnings, her small form light enough to be carried with ease. Aronious vaulted from rooftop to rooftop, his cloak snapping behind him like wings. He lashed out with his whip again, this time catching the corner of a shop sign. The wood splintered but held long enough for him to swing across a narrow alley and crash through a hanging bundle of dried herbs, scattering them in a fragrant cloud. Hobbins, now dangerously close to the tavern, decided it was time to end this race. She skidded to a halt, aimed a chromatic orb at her own chest, and unleashed the spell with reckless abandon. The orb detonated. The force hurled her backward through the air like a cannonball. She flew over a stable, past a startled dwarf loading his cart, and straight into a snowbank on the far side of the street. The impact knocked the wind from her lungs and the consciousness from her mind. Hobbins woke moments later, groggy and aching, her vision swimming. Every inch of her small body screamed in protest. She blinked snow from her whiskers and groaned, trying to piece together what had just happened. Then she saw him. Aronious swung through the air on his whip, silhouetted against the gray sky, and landed with a heavy thud just outside the entrance to The Wet Trout. He straightened, breathing hard, and reached for the door handle. No. Hobbins gritted her teeth, pushed through the pain, and forced herself to her feet. She stumbled forward, dragging herself out of the snowbank, driven by sheer stubborn will and an unquenchable thirst. Yin Shen, still in fox form and suspended by her mage hand , streaked toward the door from above. But Aronious saw her coming. His whip lashed out, coiled around her spectral grip, and yanked her sideways. She yowled in frustration as she tumbled through the air and landed in a heap beside the tavern wall. Aronious grinned, grabbed the door handle, and pulled. The door cracked open — just an inch. Hobbins squeezed through the gap. She hit the floor running, her tiny claws scrabbling against the wooden planks as she darted between boots and chair legs. Aronious dove after her, his hand outstretched, fingers grasping at air. He missed. Hobbins launched herself onto the bar, seized a shot glass that had been left unattended, and without looking or thinking — without caring what was inside — she tipped it back and downed the contents in one burning gulp. She slammed the glass down with a triumphant squeak, her chest heaving, her fur singed and dusted with snow. Victory. Aronious slumped against the bar, defeated. Yin Shen padded through the door in fox form, shifted back to her humanoid shape, and glared at both of them with a mix of exasperation and grudging respect. The bartender stared at the three of them — a ranger bent double and gasping for air, a rogue covered in snow and frost, and a ferret standing triumphantly atop his counter. "...Rough morning?" he asked. Hobbins grinned.

docs.text: Session 11: The Awakened Depths After the chaos of the morning race, Yin Shen approached the bartender at The Wet Trout and asked about blacksmiths in town. He directed her to The Coal Poker , located on the other side of Easthaven near The White Lady Inn and the town stables. Meanwhile, Hobbins bounced from table to table, asking the tavern-goers if they knew of any interesting stories or individuals looking for help from adventurers. Most were fishermen still up from the night before — red-eyed and half-asleep at their posts. But one fisherman leaned in conspiratorially and spoke of a personal encounter with a sea monster in Maer Dualdon while working as a fisher for the town of Bremen . Exhausted from their race across town, the party returned to The White Lady Inn. Hobbins and Aronious collapsed into their beds and were asleep the moment their heads touched the pillows. But Yin Shen found herself restless. She rose and made her way to The Coal Poker . Inside, she met the lead blacksmith — the largest dwarf she had ever seen, nearly human-sized but stronger and stockier. She explained that she was an investigator for the town, trying to learn all she could about Chardalyn . The blacksmith knew nothing of the material and showed clear distaste when Yin Shen mentioned the Duergar. He was not reluctant to help — merely direct and to-the-point in his speech. He muttered under his breath that it would have been nice to still have that wizard around, shame he'd turned out to be a criminal and been executed. Yin Shen confirmed he was speaking of Dzaan — the red-robed wizard the party had briefly encountered and later witnessed burn at the stake. The blacksmith's expression darkened, and he revealed something unexpected: there had been a single survivor of Dzaan's expedition. Randy Grailden , the survivor, was recovering at The White Lady Inn. The blacksmith suggested Randy might be able to show the party the way to Dzaan's tower. Yin Shen returned to the inn and found Randy in the common area, scarfing down food with barely a breath between bites. She sat down beside him without ceremony and asked outright: "What can you tell me about Dzaan?" Randy clammed up immediately, his hands beginning to shake — but he kept eating. "I don't know nothing," he stammered. "He took me, is all." Yin Shen pressed him, back and forth, until she finally convinced him that she knew he'd been to the tower, knew he'd made it back alive and alone, and knew that everyone had a price. Meekly, Randy agreed. "Fifteen gold to get out of this hell hole," he muttered to himself, "and five more to keep me comfy for a short while... yes, yes, that should do." He turned back to Yin Shen and asked for twenty gold. She paid without hesitation. Randy pulled out her map and sketched the route to Dzaan's tower with a trembling hand. Satisfied, Yin Shen finally retired to her room and slept. In the morning, the party reconnected and decided their next heading should be Bremen to investigate the monster. They hired a caravan and made the long journey, swapping between sleeping and scanning the endless, stark white landscape. When they arrived in Bremen, the party headed for the first door they saw. Hobbins barged in — and by sheer luck, the first building was the town's inn: Buried Treasures . A hearty dwarf greeted them warmly, but Hobbins cut him off, asking if he could point them toward the Speaker. The dwarf smiled, thumped his chest, and gestured to a nearby table. "Oi, I am the Speaker 'ere. Wha' tis it you're needin'?" Hobbins explained the rumor of a monster causing damage to fishing operations. The Speaker visibly relaxed, relieved to have someone take the issue seriously. He confirmed that yes, there was a monster in the lake — it was damaging boats and poaching fish. As the conversation continued, a scholarly half-elf approached and interrupted. "This isn't a monster," she said firmly. "It's a Plesiosaurus . I've been trying to study it for some time now. I'd love to get my hands on any additional information." She introduced herself as Tali . Together, the Speaker and Tali explained what they knew: the creature had a faint blue aura, appeared to be awakened, and radiated a pervasive feeling of unease whenever it was near. As the conversation wound down, Hobbins asked for the Speaker's name. With a wide, toothy grin, he replied, " Dorbulgruf Shalescar . 'Bout time we got acquainted." Hobbins then asked if there was a library in Bremen — she wanted to learn more about gods and divine energy. Dorbulgruf brought them to the town hall and opened the records room. It was sparse — just a single shelf of books — but it was enough. Hobbins leapt onto the shelves, scanning the spines until she found what she needed: Nature and the Divine . She read voraciously, learning all about divine energy and godlings. They acted as conduits, and should the vessel for divine energy be destroyed, the energy would disperse or find a new host. An idea began to form in her mind: perhaps she could funnel divine energy into Lupine . The party borrowed a rowboat from the docks and ventured out into the lake, fighting through ice floes to gather more information on the creature. Hobbins and Yin Shen found themselves near the front of the boat, providing the main paddling and thrust, while Aronious used his ranger's intuition to guide them through the crushing ice. A sudden surge of water caused a chunk of ice to smash into the hull, splintering a portion of the boat. No water came in, and the group pressed onward. They encountered a few fishing vessels here and there, steering clear of most. But one vessel from Targos shouted jeers at them, demanding they turn back. In defiance, the party continued and closed the gap. The fishermen were angry, complaining that the party was stealing fish or scaring them off. Hobbins told them all to shut their trap and tossed a gold coin into their ship. A brawl immediately erupted among the crew, all scrambling for the coin. The captain wrestled it from a crewman's hand, pocketed it, and bellowed for them to correct course and find more fish elsewhere. After more time adrift, a large wave suddenly blasted their boat, nearly tipping it over. Hobbins was quick to caution everyone that something wasn't right. Then they saw it — a large shape gliding just below the surface, testing them. The party decided to lure it toward the ice so they could stand on solid ground and ambush it. They rowed back to the ice floes and disembarked onto a large sheet of ice, hauling the boat up after them. They waited. Finally, fins broke the surface. Aronious decided to use speak with animals and called out that they had food. A long, lizard-like head lifted from the water. In clear, Common speech, it said: "I'm listening." A short conversation followed. Each additional voice seemed to agitate the beast further. The party learned that the creature had been awakened by a frost druid of Auril named Ravison . She had awakened multiple animals across Ten-Towns and commanded this one to make the people of Bremen suffer. So it had. The creature believed that if it stopped, the spell would break and it would become a mindless beast again. Hobbins, drawing on her extensive magical knowledge, was able to convince the creature that the awakening was permanent — that there was nothing binding it to this location or forcing it to obey. With that, the creature slowly descended back into the water and shot off in the opposite direction, away from Bremen. The party made their way back to town and found Speaker Dorbulgruf in his office, three empty tankards beside him and his cheeks and nose rosy with drink. He greeted them warmly and asked them to recount what happened. They explained everything. Dorbulgruf handed Hobbins a journal. "Write down whatcha learnt," he said. "The elf lass needs her notes." Hobbins scribbled furiously, her paws deft and quick. Everything they had learned was now inked onto the page. The Speaker grabbed a small bundle from another drawer. "'Ere, for the trouble," he said, handing them a Scroll of Animal Friendship and a small pouch containing five gold pieces. The party pocketed their rewards, exchanged farewells with the Speaker, and stepped back out into the frozen streets of Bremen — one mystery solved, and many more waiting in the cold.

docs.text: Session 12: The Footprints in the Snow After finishing their business in Bremen , the party decided to head to Caer-Konig . They hired a caravan to take them through the night, departing immediately. As they traveled, Aronious dozed while Hobbins rested — not fully asleep, but close. Yin Shen stayed awake, watching the road. Then the temperature dropped sharply. The stars disappeared. The world was sucked into total darkness. Streaking across the sky, barely visible against the black, Auril flew — her form casting terrible magics to keep the Rime continuing relentlessly, without mercy or end. Hobbins stirred at the sight. Rage flared in her small chest, and she thrust her paws forward, hurling magic missile at the flying visage. The arcane darts streaked upward, then faltered and faded before reaching the goddess's avatar. Auril took no notice. The caravan arrived in Caer-Konig, and the party headed for the closest building to ask directions to the Speaker or town hall. As they walked the dark street, a silver dragonborn suddenly erupted from a snowdrift, spraying snow everywhere. He swung drunkenly for Yin Shen's wrist, shouting, "Who goes there? Is it thieves? Have I found those creeping bastards?" She dodged his grasp, and the party confronted him. They asked why he'd done that and what he was hoping to accomplish. "The town's had some thievery troubles," he slurred. "No one's seen anything, really. Just the other night, the lantern over at The Northern Light was stolen. Cori won't let me hear the end of it because I haven't been able to find those responsible. Not yet, anyway. But I have a knack for this stuff." After explaining the thefts, Yin Shen asked if there was an inn nearby. The dragonborn offered to escort them there himself — and it turned out to be the very inn that had its lantern stolen. As they walked, he regaled them with tales of his time as an adventurer and how his experience made him perfectly suited to be the town's lead investigator. The party asked about the town Speaker. He spun around, grinning. "I am the town Speaker," he said proudly. "That's why I'm head investigator." When they reached the inn, Torvus opened the door and ushered them inside. The moment it swung open, a voice called from within: "Heat up something for Trovus. He's been out 'patrolling' again." He grinned sheepishly and took a seat, waiting for his meal. The party met Cori and Allie , the owners of the inn. They make it known to the party that this has become a regular event. Torvus showing up half frozen, not that he minds being a silver dragonborn, and his investigations coming up with nothing. Allie leaned in conspiratorially and said she thought it was dwarves looking for food or money. Cori scoffed. "Who's ever heard of a sneaky dwarf?" This made Yin Shen pause. She suggested it might not be a dwarf at all — but a Duergar . She told them about the party's encounter with Duergar thieves in Easthaven . When Yin Shen mentioned the footprints in the jail cell that grew progressively smaller before disappearing, Allie's face went white. She asked the party to follow her to the back entrance behind the storeroom. There, in the snow, were the same kind of footprints — leading away from the inn, growing smaller and smaller before reaching the road and vanishing into the other foot traffic. Yin Shen asked Allie to write down her account and provide her name as valid testimony for the conspiracy. While Yin Shen was distracted investigating, Hobbins caught Cori's attention. She pointed with her small paws at a bottle on the top shelf and made the largest, most innocent eyes possible. "Could I try that clear liquid up there?" Cori, utterly unprepared for such an assault, was no match. She began pouring a glass. Aronious spotted Hobbins out of the corner of his eye and darted over, smacking the small glass from her paws. Hobbins reacted instantly, tossing the glass back toward her mouth in a desperate attempt to catch even a drop. Aronious was too quick — he slapped it away mid-air. Hobbins got nothing more than a single drop on her tongue. Cori, without a word, held out a rag and pointed at the wet floor with a stern expression. Aronious shrank under her gaze and began cleaning his mess. Cori and Allie offered the party free room and board while they investigated the missing lantern. They didn't have money to offer as a reward, but recovering the lantern would not only help them — it would help repair the town's trust in Trovus and restore Caer-Konig's sense of security. The party agreed to investigate. They needed lodging anyway, and they were already planning to head northeast to explore the location marked on the map Yin Shen had bargained for. They decided to rest for the night and rise early to begin. In the morning, Yin Shen and Aronious went out to buy gear for their wilderness expedition. Hobbins decided to stay behind at the inn. The two headed to Frozenfar Expeditions — the best adventuring outfitter in the region, according to Trovus. As they stepped outside, they realized they were the first ones awake. A fresh layer of snow blanketed the ground, and a single set of footprints wound through the streets — not entering any buildings, but moving from window to window, door to door, slipping between alleyways. Yin Shen compared them to the prints from the inn and from Easthaven. She was confident: these were Duergar tracks. The two followed the trail. It led to the northernmost edge of town, where it stopped in an area that looked like a dogsled had been waiting. The footprints ended there — but two very large footprints continued away from town, accompanied by dogsled tracks. Yin Shen decided it was still best to visit Frozenfar Expeditions first before continuing the investigation. At the outfitter, Yin Shen negotiated the rental of a dogsled, along with food, water, and all necessary supplies for roughly ten days of travel. She put down a deposit and arranged for training on how to operate the sled. With their preparations complete, they returned to the inn to gather Hobbins and ready themselves for their trek into the wilderness. The footprints waited in the snow. The Duergar conspiracy was unraveling thread by thread. And somewhere to the northeast, in the frozen wastes beyond Caer-Konig, Dzaan's tower awaited — along with whatever secrets the mad wizard had left behind.

docs.text: Session 13: The Dragon and the Stronghold The party left Caer-Konig fully stocked with winter adventuring gear, following the large footprints and dogsled tracks into the wilderness. As they traveled, the wind and snow picked up dramatically, reducing visibility to almost nothing. The Rime was fighting back. The party pressed on for hours through rolling, snow-covered hills before cresting a larger rise. In the distance, they spotted a ravine — and in the clearing at its center lay the back half of a polar bear, seemingly taken by a single bite. Deciding to pause and scan the area for threats, they heard a low, rumbling sound. The snowdrift on the far wall of the ravine shifted and fell away in a small avalanche, revealing the massive head and neck of an ancient white dragon . Aronious took a closer look and saw a saddle peeking out of the snow. Strapped in place was a robed figure, half-buried and unmoving — head slumped, arms hanging limp at its sides. Hobbins had heard tales of an ancient white dragon during her time in Ten-Towns but had never had reason to believe them until now. The three exchanged a glance and decided to continue on their way as quietly as possible, careful not to disturb the sleeping wyrm. After more travel through the frozen wastes, the party arrived at the base of Kelvin's Cairn . They quickly hid the dogsled and concealed their presence, then noticed a stronghold carved directly into the stone of the mountain. The party regrouped, loaded their prizes onto the dogsled, and began their trek back to Caer-Konig. Behind them, the stronghold sat silent and cold — its secrets partially uncovered, its conspiracy laid bare. Ahead, the lights of the town flickered faintly through the storm. And somewhere beneath the ice, a father plotted. His doom would soar on dragon's wings.

docs.text: Session 14: The Return to Easthaven The party left the Duergar stronghold with the Duergar leader bound to the dogsled, stolen goods from Caer-Konig piled on top of him. The two rescued goats were tied to the sled, making the journey back slow and cumbersome. As they passed the ravine where they had seen the ancient white dragon slumbering, they noticed the wyrm was no longer visible — its massive form appeared to have been re-buried by fresh snowdrifts. They returned to Caer-Konig, and Aronious and Yin Shen took the prisoner and the magical color-changing lantern to The Northern Light to meet with the town Speaker and return the stolen goods. Hobbins was left with the dogsled at the north end of town. With the sled caretakers gone, the dogs became restless and began to wander. Hobbins' small body had little effect on the reins, and the dogs moved of their own accord down the streets of Caer-Konig. With squeaks and yelps, she wrestled with the leather cords and pulled with all her might to guide them back to their kennel. The kennel master saw this unfold and walked out to greet her. Hobbins asked him to watch their things, tossed him a copper coin, and ran off to catch up with the party. Allie and Cori were thrilled to see their lantern again but apologized for their lack of coin. They rummaged through their belongings and handed over a small purse containing only three gold and six silver pieces. "We're sorry we don't have more to offer you," Cori said sadly. "Times is rough with the winter's Rime shuttering travel, trade, and the joy in our hearts. This is all we have left." "We can offer you rooms and food free of charge whenever you visit!" Allie quickly added. The conversation then turned to the prisoner. Yin Shen explained the situation at the frozen stronghold. Torvus was shocked to hear of such a grand conspiracy. "And here I thought I was looking for petty thieves," he muttered, taking a long pull from his wine bottle. Yin Shen asked if he would be willing to speak to other town Speakers and help them understand the threat. "I can do you one better!" Trovus exclaimed. "Cori! Quill and parchment, if you don't mind." Despite the drink, his hand was steady and his words clear. In short order, he drafted a legal document deputizing the party as agents of Caer-Konig , placing them as direct reports to the town Speaker. "This should go a long way in proving you've got our backing," he said, rolling his signet ring in the wax seal. Yin Shen stored the writ safely in her bag, then asked if he could help with the cost of travel in the area — she suspected they had a lot of journeying ahead. Trovus dug through his heavy furs and fine Speaker's clothing, emptying pockets onto the counter. He pulled out four separate half-empty containers of alcohol before producing what he was looking for. "Ahh, here we are." He handed Yin Shen another slip — a Torg's Trading Company Travel Voucher . Fine print indicated it was valid for Eastway travel but did not service Lonelywood or Dugan's Hole. "That should go a ways for you," he said. "It's no silver bullet, but it'll get you across Ten-Towns no problem." The party left the inn and returned to where Hobbins had left the sled. When they arrived, the sled was packed away, the dogs were kenneled and resting, and their goods sat on a pallet waiting for them. The porter was dozing in a chair nearby, hat resting over his eyes. Aronious took immediate issue with this slothful behavior. He scolded the porter about the risk of thieves while he slept, then accused him of being a thief himself — that this was all part of a plan to cheat them. The porter, confused, apologized profusely for his lack of professionalism. "You're right, sir! I should never have gone lax once my work was done!" Aronious continued berating the man until Hobbins stepped in and said they needed to leave. "You're right, Hobbins, we do need to leave," Aronious declared. "But not before I leave a terrible review on Gelp !" The party made their way to the caravan office and, after some trouble proving ownership of the voucher, secured free passage to Easthaven . Yin Shen stayed alert the entire journey to ensure their prisoner did not escape. Once in Easthaven, they went straight to the town hall. There, they met Captain Imdra Arlaggath and presented her not only with a new prisoner but also with the signed and sealed document from Trovus. Yin Shen explained the conspiracy in full. Everything aligned with the thieves who had previously escaped from Easthaven. She unfolded the letter they had found, which stated the Duergar were using the Easthaven Ferry as a base of operations. Imdra saw the looming threat clearly and believed them. She promised to send notices to all town Speakers and to do what she could to prepare — though she warned it would take time, as not everyone moved as quickly as she did. Yin Shen asked if they could be deputized in the same way they had been in Caer-Konig. Imdra held out her hand for Trovus' document, read it, then wrote that while not formally deputized, the party was working under official business of Captain Imdra and Easthaven . She signed it and pressed her signet into wax. The party decided it was time to visit the music shop owner. They first went to Drums Emporium . The door was closed and locked. No lights shone from inside. The shelves were empty, and dust motes floated in the air. The back room door hung askew, its interior shadowed in darkness. Aronious kicked down the door in fear and haste. He barged in, shocked by the emptiness, then rushed to the back workshop area. It too was clean — no wood shavings, no metal dust. The broken trapdoor had been replaced with seamless, newly installed flooring. The party panicked and ran full speed to Strings and Sundries . Lights glowed inside, and instruments lined the shelves. Aronious attempted to kick this door down as well, but his boot bounced off and he hurt his ankle. He readied his other leg when Yin Shen tried the doorknob. The door swung open just as Aronious kicked — and he fell forward into the shop. The shopkeeper was a tall, slender woman in a red dress. She was startled to see them tumble inside. "Oh! Umm, may I help you?" The party frantically skipped formalities, wanting to know where the gnome was. She giggled and explained she was the new store manager — the gnome owner had decided to step back from day-to-day operations. "He's probably at home, behind the workshop. You can find him there." The party sprinted to his home. Aronious charged forward, leg readied to kick down the door. Yin Shen knelt and pulled out lockpicking tools, working on the lock. Hobbins scrambled with her little paws, trying to squeeze through gaps in the doorframe. After much commotion and little success, the door finally opened from the inside. Polard Hinscrop stood in the doorway, hands on his hips, looking annoyed. "What are you guys doing here?" They explained they had gone on a short trip north and had returned to see how he was doing. "I waited for you to come back and take me on an adventure," he said accusingly, "and now I find you went on one without me!" The party apologized profusely, saying they'd gotten things mixed up — they thought he needed more time to think it over. He forgave them, their apologies seeming sincere. The party immediately invited him to join them. Polard scurried into his house. Sitting on a chair at the dining room table was a fully handmade suit of armor: the helmet was a metal pasta strainer, the shoulder pads were bent cymbals, and the rest was a hodgepodge of kitchen utensils, musical instrument components, and leather straps. He put everything on, then disappeared and reappeared with a backpack twice his size. "Ready to go!" The party decided to visit the smith. They had heard the dwarves there were able to enchant materials. Once there, they learned the dwarves didn't do the enchanting themselves — they had connections and shipped goods off for arcane modification before re-importing them to sell. They acted as middlemen, and it was good for business to keep those connections secret. The party was determined to get Polard better armor, convinced his homemade gear wouldn't be sufficient. The dwarves inspected it and were genuinely impressed by the craftsmanship. Sure, it looked silly — but they promised it was well-made and would stop a blade. After some bartering, Hobbins offered to teach one of the dwarven apprentices — the one most adept at magic — how to use the arcane to reinforce the edge of a mundane metal sword. In exchange, the dwarves would provide one steel helmet free of charge. Yin Shen took the opportunity to purchase some caltrops as well. Aronious decided to investigate the local fletcher. He entered and saw a solitary elf — tall but lacking the usual elegance associated with his kind. He was heavyset with a bushy gray beard, lazily attaching feathers to an arrow shaft and barely lifting his eyes when Aronious entered. Most of the bows were regular or mundane, but there was a section with intricately carved scrimshaw on bone reinforcing the limbs. The price was steep — far beyond what Aronious could afford. After a brief discussion with the shopkeeper, Hobbins walked in and browsed alongside Aronious. She saw the bone reinforcement and asked about it. He explained it made the bow stronger, and if they could provide materials, the fletcher would only charge for labor. Hobbins reached into her bag and pulled out the frost giant bone she had been holding onto. She placed it on the shopkeeper's table. "Will this work?" she asked sweetly. The elf's eyes went wide. "By the gods, is this... giant's bone?" He held his hands over it and used arcane magic to identify the material. "Frost giant's bone. Incredible." His face, previously stoic and uninterested, was now alight with joy and determination. "Get out of my shop at once! Return in one week — I will have a bow the likes of which you have never seen." The party saw the flames in his eyes and did not argue. The moment they stepped outside, they heard frantic movement, the click of locks, and the slamming of wooden shutters. The fletcher's shop was now closed.

docs.text: Session 15: The Black Spire The week following the showdown at the Duergar stronghold passed quietly. Hobbins spent her days in structured routine — visiting the dwarven smith each morning to train the young apprentice she had taken under her wing. Aronious spent his days doing something rather different: pacing. He had commissioned a bow. He knew it was coming. He simply could not stop thinking about it. On the morning the week ended, Aronious was standing at the fletcher's door before the sun had properly crested the horizon. Hobbins arrived moments later, breath fogging in the cold air. The fletcher presented his work: a Giant's Bone longbow , ivory white and immaculate. Intricate scrimshaw wound in delicate patterns along the full length of the limbs, and golden thread wrapped the grip with care. That same golden thread served as the bowstring itself, catching the faint morning light with a faint shimmer. Aronious was speechless — briefly. Hobbins had arranged a trade with the blacksmith: her services for a helmet for Polard , who could use something more substantial than a metal pasta strainer between his head and trouble. With new weapons, new gear, and renewed purpose, the party regrouped and made their way to the Easthaven town hall. Captain Imdra Arlaggath had news. The scouts she had dispatched returned during the week with their report: out in the frozen wilderness, near the location marked by the man at the inn, there was something . What exactly, they could not say. Only that it was there, and it was not natural. The party didn't need long to deliberate. They booked passage on the caravan north to Caer-Konig and geared up at Frozenfar Expeditions , loading a dogsled with supplies for the cold and the unknown. Before setting out, Yin Shen produced the scroll of fireball that once belonged to Dzaan . Rather than saving it for a fight, she had the scent of the scroll carried to the sled dogs — giving them something to track out into the white expanse. The tundra was unforgiving. The wind cut at their faces and the hills rolled endlessly in every direction, an ocean of white frozen mid-swell. Without landmarks, miles began to blur together. It wasn't long before a disagreement broke out over which direction they were actually heading. The debate grew heated — and then physical, when Hobbins settled the matter by throwing herself bodily onto the reins. The sled dogs veered hard to the right, and the argument was over. What wasn't over was the terrain. As the sled crested the hill Hobbins had chosen, the party realized it was no hill at all — it was the lip of a cliff, dropping away into a ravine below. All three immediately threw their weight to the opposite side and hauled on the reins with everything they had. The sled swung, the dogs yelped and corrected, and the cliff edge passed beneath them by a margin none of them wanted to think about. As they put the ravine behind them, low growls and distant shrieks drifted across the wind — sounds like something between an animal and a human voice. They pressed on. The growls returned some time later, closer now. The sled dogs began to slow. From the windswept snow emerged three Crag Cats — massive, pale, nearly invisible against the blizzard backdrop. They moved with predatory patience, stalking the sled as if they had been following it for some time. The cats struck fast, bounding in and out of range with terrifying precision. But the party was faster to recover. Blade and arcane power drove the creatures back — one fell to the combined assault of steel and magic. docs.text: Session 16: The Lifespark and the Machine The party descended through the black spire's lower opening and dropped into what had once been a wizard's laboratory — broken glass, scattered alchemical gear, and shelves long since emptied by time and ruin. From an adjacent chamber, Yin Shen heard low voices: one robed figure speaking to an undead attendant, muttering over parchment about failed experiments and a missing lifespark . Creeping closer without entering, she heard him slam his hands down in frustration: "Dammit — all experiments failed. I need a lifespark." After a tense whisper-circle, the party chose introductions over violence. Yin Shen knocked on the doorway before stepping in. The robed figure turned — and the party recoiled. It was Dzaan , the same wizard Yin Shen had seen burned at the stake in Easthaven, though this one shimmered at the edges like heat-haze. "Ahh! Visitors! I am Dzaan... or almost," he said. He explained that he was a simulacrum: incomplete, unstable, and separate from the original wizard's memories after his creation. He claimed ignorance of the execution and the crimes tied to Dzaan's name, then pointed them toward an ancient Netherese device below that could make him fully corporeal — Dzaan in body, not merely likeness. As payment, he offered the medallion on his worktable. Yin Shen pushed further, negotiating for all information he possessed on chardalyn in addition to the amulet. Dzaan agreed. The party agreed. "Just a warning before going further, there are a few experiments below. Do avoid using acid, cold, or lightning while down there!" At the next level down, Dzaan's warning proved true. Black slimes surged from the darkness and attacked with acid-soaked pseudopods. The battle was brutal and close. Aronious's wolf was left badly burned, and Hobbins unleashed Aganazzar's scorcher in a desperate counterattack that melted through multiple oozes — but left her exposed. The final slime slammed her to the ground, unconscious and sizzling from acid burns. Aronious and his wolf finished the last ooze while Yin Shen stabilized Hobbins. Against the odds, the party survived and pressed forward. In a ruined bedchamber nearby, they found the corpse of a long-dead wizard and something stranger still: an invisible, locked chest hidden among the rubble. Yin Shen failed to pick the lock, so Hobbins improvised. She had Aronious hold the unseen chest aloft while she blasted the lock with chromatic orb . The lock shattered and fell away. Inside was a leather-bound book. The moment Yin Shen removed it, it crumbled instantly to ash. Hobbins identified the chest as a magical container that held contents in temporal stasis — airtight, watertight, and fixed at a constant temperature. Outside the chest, the book experienced roughly two thousand years of age in moments. Deciding she was in no shape for another fight, Hobbins climbed inside for safety and pulled the lid shut. The party, accompanied by Dzaan and his undead companion, reached the chamber of the Netherese machine. Runes were etched across the walls and apparatus, but deep cracks ran through the stone, and the inscriptions flickered with instability. When asked to identify the runes, Hobbins could only confirm they were ancient Netherese and beyond modern understanding. Dzaan took position on the central platform and instructed Yin Shen to touch the pedestal. She did. A golden bolt leapt from her hand into the machine. Runes ignited in blue and gold, the chamber roared to life, and arcane energy spiraled around Dzaan. Then everything went wrong. Krintas shoved the party out of the chamber as the vortex destabilized. The chest spilled open and Hobbins burst back into the chaos, demanding the door be opened. She blasted it apart with chromatic orb just as radiant energy erupted from the machine in a violent flash. Aronious reacted in time to slam the chest shut again, but Yin Shen and Aronious were struck by radiant bolts, and Krintas took the worst of it — hurled into a wall, flesh scorched and smoldering. When the light faded, the machine wound down. Dzaan stepped forward, now fully corporeal. He handed over the promised amulet. After tense questioning, the party tested Dzaan for fiendish influence. Hobbins, still under detect good and evil , saw no demonic taint on him. They chose trust over conflict. Dzaan agreed to travel with the party alongside Krintas. Hobbins agreed to share her spell knowledge to help rebuild his spellbook, and Dzaan offered to teach Yin Shen magic. The group returned to the surface and reunited with Polard Hinscrop , who was disappointed to have missed the danger below. Then Hobbins asked the question no one had dared speak aloud: Why not use the machine again? The entire party turned around and descended once more. Back in the chamber, they found the damage worsening — cracks spreading, runes flickering, the structure nearing collapse. Hobbins judged there might only be one or two uses left. They decided Yin Shen needed a ranged weapon. She created a detailed minor illusion of a blowgun with poisoned and sleep-laced darts, and Hobbins activated the pedestal. The machine hummed, this time without the catastrophic radiant backlash. A real blowgun and real darts clattered onto the stone floor. "One use left, maybe," Hobbins warned. The party fell silent, already planning what final creation might be worth the risk.

docs.text: Session 17: Masks, Militia, and Old Tracks The party stood in the shadow of the inverted spire and made a difficult choice: they would save the machine's final use for another day. Before leaving, Yin Shen pointed out a practical problem. Dzaan , now fully corporeal, could not simply walk into Easthaven wearing his old face and name. Aronious solved the second problem immediately. "Gustavo," he said. Yin Shen solved the first with steel, dye, and determination. She shaved Dzaan clean, cut his hair short, took his pointed hat, and turned his red scarf blue. When she finished, Dzaan sat slumped in a chair, clutching the newly dyed cloth like a funeral token. "Why did it have to be blue..." The climb out of the spire was slow and awkward, but at last the ropes and climbing gear bought from Frozenfar Expeditions earned their keep. Aronious hauled Hobbins in the temporal chest and laughed through gritted teeth about finally getting some use out of all that equipment. On the sled ride back, the tundra offered a moment of impossible stillness. A herd of reindeer crossed a clearing under night sky and snowlight. Two great stags walked guard at the edges, antlers igniting with pale radiance as an aurora unfurled above them. One deer lingered behind and met Aronious's gaze. It did not flee when he approached. It lowered its head as he reached out. For a breath, hunter and herd touched spirits. Aronious felt something answer him in the cold: a bond, old and wild, and the promise that if he called in need, the herd might hear. Back in Easthaven, the party sought answers about the temporal chest. Hobbins first brought it to a dwarven smith, who inspected it with practical interest and offered scrap value on the spot. "Could make a breastplate or two from that." Hobbins threw herself between the smith and the chest so quickly she nearly tripped over it, apologizing and refusing the sale. She wanted to know what else it could do before anyone melted it down. On the way out, she spotted the apprentice she had been training, surrounded by scorched practice pieces and smoking rune-plates. His progress was visible. So was the amount of work left. As they moved through Easthaven's frozen streets, a dark-robed stranger slipped from the crowd and pressed a violet paper into their hands. "The Violet Hold Inn may have what you seek. They specialize in moving objects of power." He tried to vanish immediately. Yin Shen and Hobbins stopped him, pulled his hood down, and found only a hunched, elderly courier who knew just enough to be suspicious and not enough to be useful. The party let him go with more questions than answers. They brought their concerns to Captain Imdra Arlaggath . Her face fell before they had even finished asking about the duergar prisoner. The prisoner had hidden chardalyn shards on his person. In confinement he drove those shards into his own flesh, and whatever demonic force lived in the crystal devoured what remained of his mind. By the time the guards intervened, he had become something feral and unrecognizable. They put him down. Imdra accepted responsibility for another failed interrogation and asked forgiveness. Then she shared broader news: three more towns had begun reinforcing militia and preparing for a threat no one could yet name. Half of Ten-Towns now stood in varying states of readiness. She continued pressing the rest. With the prison lead gone, the party turned to the amulet from the black spire and the construct it was meant to command: the lost shield guardian. They took a caravan east to west along the Ten-Towns routes until Bremen , the farthest point their ride would carry them. During the journey, Dzaan barely slept, eyes bloodshot as he obsessively reconstructed his spellbook from memory whenever the sled or wagon stopped jolting enough to write. Yin Shen studied Netherese history and chardalyn lore whenever there was light to read by. At Bremen, Aronious found another expedition shack: a weather-beaten structure and an elderly owner with a pipe, a sales pitch, and a sled that looked one hard turn away from becoming firewood. The haggling was spirited. The salesman promised the rig had gone thousands of miles and patted the frame, which answered by dropping a loose piece of timber into the snow. Aronious offered one gold for half ownership instead of a rental. The owner accepted. Hobbins refused to put life or limb on that sled now that they technically owned part of it. She tracked down a carpenter and commissioned a fresh build for eight gold. By day's end, the party had a new sled, a small dog team, and a direction. They set their sights on the wilderness again, hunting the trail of a forgotten Netherese guardian.

docs.text: Session 18: The Goblin's Crown The new sled creaked and the six scrawny dogs strained against their leads as the party pushed out of Bremen and into the open tundra. The amulet in Aronious 's hands pulsed with direction, a steady tug toward the mountains like a compass needle finding north. The snow came down thick and fast. A blizzard rolled in without warning, reducing the world to a white wall pressing in on all sides. The party pressed on regardless, guided more by the amulet's pull than by any sense of where the land ended and the sky began. After some time, a glow materialized in the white distance — faint at first, then unmistakable. Curiosity won out, and the sled veered toward it. The light resolved into a torch held aloft by a stout dwarven figure trudging through waist-deep drifts with the single-minded energy of a man on a mission he's thoroughly enjoying. He was barrel-chested, trailing a long red beard packed with snow, and strapped across his back was a peculiar device — a metal tube mounted in a wooden frame, a hemp wick hanging from the end. None of them recognized the contraption. He greeted them with the enthusiasm of someone who had been alone in a blizzard too long and found it wholly acceptable. His name was Mylbor Tarrfak — a trophy hunter with a cabin to the northeast, currently in pursuit of a Red Yeti that had been making a nuisance of itself in the area. The device on his back, he explained with some pride, was his "Thunder Stick" — a single shot, but one that packed a punch. He offered the party a wager: three hundred gold if they could find the Yeti before he did. They declined. Yin Shen asked if he had any interest in hunting a dragon instead. Mylbor's eyes lit — then dimmed slightly when she described the Chardalyn Dragon as a construct. He was on the verge of losing interest entirely when she mentioned Duergar. The color rose in his face like a tide. "That certainly sweetens the deal." They agreed to reconnect in two days at the tavern in Bremen, and his torch faded to a dim amber point behind the curtain of snow. The amulet led the party onward toward the mountains. The terrain shifted, the wind dropping as they descended into a ravine carved into the rock — sheltered from the storm above, growing darker as the walls rose around them. The sky narrowed to a pale strip overhead. The ravine opened without warning into an interior clearing. Goblin construction sprawled across it — watchtowers, timber walls, the whole crude architecture of a settlement dug in and making itself permanent. The guards at their posts were paying far more attention to the braziers beside them than to the perimeter they were supposed to be watching. Aronious could feel the Shield Guardian somewhere at the center. Yin Shen decided the most efficient path was the direct one. She walked toward the gates as though she had every right to be there — until an arrow snapped into the ground in front of her feet and a goblin voice demanded to know her business, with the clear implication that the next shot would not be aimed at the dirt. She announced they were expected. The effect was immediate. The goblin ran. Yellow eyes narrowed at them from the walls as bows were drawn — and then the great gates groaned open to reveal a larger goblin astride a worg, studying them with the measured expression of someone weighing a decision. "Are you the emissaries?" Yin Shen agreed that they were. Behind her, Polard Hinscrop was vibrating. Hobbins asked what was wrong. He explained, in a frantic whisper, that goblins and gnomes were natural enemies — that the moment they got a proper look at him, things would go sideways in a hurry. Hobbins climbed to his shoulders and wrapped him in a disguise: not ideal, but a dwarf was better odds than a gnome. They were escorted inside. At the center of the stronghold, the Shield Guardian hung from rope and timber like a puppet with its strings cut — massive, still, and waiting. Hobbins broke from the group and slipped unseen toward it while the rest continued to the chief's building, Yin Shen taking up the thread of the disguise as Hobbins moved away. The chief's hall was dim, and the goblin who occupied it was a peculiar specimen — unsettling in ways that were hard to place. He led them into a room he called the "chatting chamber" and closed the door behind them. Then he reached up and pulled off his head. Beneath the goblin mask was a gnome — lean, harried, and profoundly relieved to see someone who wasn't a goblin. He reintroduced himself as Spellix Romwood , a merchant whose caravan had been ambushed in the mountain pass to the west. His goods were gone, his people taken, and he had fashioned a goblin disguise to try to free them. Somehow — through a series of events he described as "immediately going wrong in every direction" — he had stumbled into the role of chief. docs.text: Session 19: Thunder, Ale, and the Dragon's Answer The party returned to Bremen with Spellix Romwood in tow, the Shield Guardian stomping along behind them — its iron frame still covered head to toe in goblin graffiti. Spellix thanked them with genuine warmth, explained he would be staying at the inn briefly before heading south to his family, then turned out his pockets to reveal they were entirely empty. He shrugged. Perhaps the inn was too much to hope for. Aronious pressed two gold into his hand without a word. Rest, at least, would come easy. Dzaan was sent ahead to the inn as well. He walked through the door, sat down at the nearest table, and immediately began scrawling in his spellbook with the focused desperation of a man racing against his own memory. He did not look up. Yin Shen remarked that it was past time they all rested — everyone had taken a beating. Hobbins and Aronious turned to look at her with the flat, unified expression of two people covered in bruises regarding someone without a single mark on them. Yin Shen said nothing further. Before rest could be considered, Hobbins had unfinished business. The Shield Guardian stood in the street where they had left it, patient and enormous and absolutely covered in goblin scrawl. She was not willing to leave it that way. The party browsed the shelves of the local market, where they found a bottle of Grizwald's Famous Degreaser with the tagline: It'll remove anything and everything. The clerk admitted, without any apparent shame, that it was in fact terrible at removing grease but cut through paint as though it had never existed. Too harsh. They put it back. Instead they selected green, pink, purple, and black paint and a set of brushes, and set about the rather more delicate work of making the construct look less like a siege weapon and more like something a person might not immediately flee from. Hobbins applied the finishing touch herself: a pink peace symbol, carefully painted across the Guardian's forehead. It helped. Somewhat. Yin Shen suggested, again, that they head inside to rest. Aronious made only a token effort to stop Hobbins from lunging at Yin Shen's ankles, his grip conspicuously loose as the ferret squeaked about not a single arrow having touched her, about bruises, about the Shield Guardian nearly being destroyed. The scuffle resolved itself in time, and the party made for their rooms. They had barely started up the stairs when the door burst open. Mylbor Tarrfak filled the frame, crimson-stained sack slung over one shoulder and Thunder Stick raised in one hand — or what remained of it. The end had mushroomed outward into a tangle of singed and curling metal. He grinned the grin of a man who had fired his only shot and found it sufficient. "Only took one shot," he said, dropping the sack on the floor with a wet thud. "Though I only had one shot." A hearty laugh filled the room. He threw his coin purse onto the bar before anyone could object, ordered a round, and passed tankards to Yin Shen and Aronious. Aronious, with careful deliberation, poured a bottle cap's worth of clear liquor for Hobbins. They raised their drinks. Mylbor drained his in a single pull and looked around the table with the expectant expression of a man waiting to be matched. Aronious, reasoning that a sufficiently drunk Mylbor might prove a more cooperative ally, accepted the implied challenge. He seized a full bottle of clear liquor and poured it down without pause. Mylbor turned to the barmaid and asked what that equated to in ale. She said a full cask. Mylbor's eyes lit up. He was already behind the bar and on the floor before anyone thought to stop him. Yin Shen grabbed the handle of the keg and opened it. Mylbor sputtered, drank, gulped, and sputtered again — and eventually, with great reluctance, tapped the floor. He stood slowly, thumped his chest, and produced a belch of considerable authority. "You win, laddy." Yin Shen suggested it was time for everyone to sleep. Hobbins, no longer able to contain herself on the subject of Yin Shen's perfect, unmarked, unscathed person, launched herself across the room. The scuffle was brief. Things settled. The party went to bed. They rose early, waited for Mylbor to surface, and found him in reasonable shape for a man who had consumed a cask of ale. Over breakfast, he and Yin Shen came to an agreement: they would stay in contact. She wanted word of the ancient white dragon that roamed Icewind Dale. He wanted word of anything worth hunting. Both parties shook on it and parted ways. The road to Termalaine ate most of the day, and the party arrived in the evening to find a large orc in fine clothing standing in the street barking orders at a cluster of civilians doing their best impression of a town militia. Most of them looked as though they had never held a weapon before last week. He turned when the party approached. They explained they were working under Captain Imdra Arlaggath and were looking for the town Speaker. "You've found him," he said, and introduced himself as Oarus Masthew . Imdra's warning had reached him, and he had wasted no time. Every able-bodied person in Termalaine who could hold a spear was now, in some technical sense, a soldier. The party left him to it. Finding a quiet corner to think, the group turned to a question that had been waiting long enough: the ancient white dragon. Yin Shen was confident. White dragons, she explained, were benevolent creatures. They enjoyed the company of people. Hobbins composed herself, reached for the magic of sending , and pushed the message outward into the cold. "Don't panic, we are friendly, need help, Ten-Towns in danger, meet at Redwaters, Lupine can vouch, at sundown in two days. Ciao!" The answer came back low and rasping, like stone grinding against stone. "Come to my lair at the Sea of Moving Ice. You'll find a shipwreck I use as one of my homes." Two days of travel, at minimum. The direction was vague. The invitation was not the kind one declined. As they moved through Termalaine's streets turning the logistics over in their minds, a posting on the Gelp board stopped them short. Written in urgent, uneven letters: Miners Lost! 50g Reward. Below it, in smaller text, a note that the local miners' guild had refused all work until the lost men were found and the mine declared safe. Fifty gold was fifty gold. They looked at one another, looked at the road stretching north toward the Sea of Moving Ice, and thought about it for a longer moment than any of them would readily admit. The dragon was waiting. They turned up their collars and walked back out into the cold.

docs.text: Session 2: The Many Whispers in Easthaven When the travelers returned to the Trail's End Tavern , the night was calm and cold, and the road behind them lay silent. Yet one thing was amiss — Torg's Company was gone, their sleds and dogs no where to be seen. Left while the part was away. As they pondered their next course, the tavern door opened, letting in a gust of frost and a figure robed in rusty brown and red — Dzaan . His eyes sparkled with curiosity rather than menace, and a hint of a smile tugged at his lips. “Adventurers, by the look of you,” he said, striding to their table. “I’m conducting research on the elemental spirits that dwell in this land — Chwingas , I believe the locals call them. Elusive little things. I would pay handsomely for their study.” Behind him, a companion in studded leather lingered at the doorway, but before the group could take a good look, the door shut and the figure was gone. Dzaan placed a small lantern of gentle blue fire upon the table. “This,” he explained, “is attuned to the spirits. It glows when they are near. Bring me one, and twenty-five gold is yours.” Hobbins' eager chatter — and Yin Shen's foxlike grin — saw the wizard laugh and raise the offer. “A fine bit of negotiation,” he admitted, “and a sign of capable company. Thirty gold pieces it is.” The party accepted and returned to the forest, lantern in hand. There, beneath the whispering pines, they sought to coax the Chwingas from hiding. Remembering the tales that the spirits were fond of childish wonder, the group began to dance, sing, and play at circles in the snow — ring around the rosy beneath the moonlight. It was a comical sight: Aronious trying, with some dignity, to keep pace; Yin Shen spinning with genuine delight; and Hobbins darting through the snow like a ribbon of fur and laughter. Yet for all their effort, no spirit appeared. The lantern’s flame flickered once, then stilled. With frost clinging to their cloaks and little gained for their play, they decided to continue their travels east to Easthaven . By the time they arrived, the sky was black and heavy with snow. The lamps of The White Lady Inn shone dimly through the storm — a welcome sight. Inside, warmth and music greeted them, and a bard named Rinaldo was making his rounds, filling the room with song and stories of the inn’s spectral namesake. The trio took their rest there. The next day as they warmed themselves by the hearth, a bard named Rinaldo approached — a man of quick fingers and quicker tongue — proclaiming that he would hold a séance to summon the spirit of the inn’s namesake, the White Lady who drowned long ago beneath the frozen lake. Yin Shen ventured into the square, where she stumbled upon a grim spectacle — Dzaan , the very wizard who had so warmly hired them, bound to a stake as the townsfolk gathered round. The flames climbed swiftly, and he met his end with unsettling calm. Beside Yin Shen stood Captain Imdra Arlaggath , the stern leader of Easthaven’s guard. Seeing her disquiet, the captain muttered, “Do not pity him, stranger. He murdered those he hired — folk of Icewind Dale — after they aided his travels. He’s reaping what he sowed.” When the captain turned her questioning gaze to Yin Shen , the rogue answered plainly that she and her companions had only crossed Dzaan’s path briefly, and were in fact hunting Sephek Kaltro , the killer who had plagued Ten-Towns. Hearing that the murderer was no more, the captain’s demeanor softened. “You’ve a sharp eye and a steady hand,” she said. “We’ve fishermen gone missing out on the ice. Find them, and what Dzaan carried in life shall be yours in death.” The reward, as it turned out, included a Scroll of Fireball and a curious Gray Bag of Tricks , both lightly scorched from the pyre.
